summary: Submitted draft/submission.json (action=obligation) opening a second, independent responsibility in the captured hashicorp/raft snapshot after the first obligation was confirmed in scope. The submission carries a handoff feedback that records the answered proposition (the confirmed term-context regression) together with the remaining discriminators (vote-record escalation, known-leader rollback) so the settled premise is not re-investigated; no map version was created, keeping the frontier wording cleanup for the next map submission that actually needs it. The new Candidate is about client-request completion against an inactive node: Raft.VerifyLeader, ApplyLog and Barrier each select between an already-closed shutdownCh and a send on an internal request channel, so with buffer space both cases are ready and the request can be enqueued after shutdown was signalled; nothing drains verifyCh or applyCh once run, fsm and snapshot goroutines have exited (shutdownFuture waits on the goroutine group) and deferError only consults ShutdownCh, which neither logFuture nor verifyFuture ever sets, so the returned future blocks forever in Error() while ErrRaftShutdown is documented as the result for operations against an inactive Raft and the in-repo after-shutdown test asserts that everything should fail. The claim c-client-request-completes-on-inactive-raft is classified bounded_liveness, uses principal fact f-known-leader with the consumption lifecycle, cites b-client-apply-verify (A7) and b-leader-identity (A2) with b-leader-lease-stepdown and b-heartbeat-fastpath as support, and is bound by bind-raft-verify-leader at api.go VerifyLeader (lines 883-893, declaration verified), with 12 new source ranges covering the selects, the 64-slot verifyCh, the BatchApplyCh buffering, deferError, shutdownFuture, waitShutdown, the run loop's shutdown return, the main-loop verify handler and the in-repo test comment. A construction-time probe of the captured source measured 64 of 128 VerifyLeader calls made after a completed Shutdown() returning futures still unresolved after a bounded wait, 54 to 74 of 128 Apply calls with BatchApplyCh=true likewise, and Barrier with the default unbuffered applyCh returning ErrRaftShutdown 8 of 8 times, which shows the failure follows from the channel being buffered rather than from the API; that probe is recorded as construction knowledge, not as formal evidence, and the obligation presumes no violation. Counterevidence is kept explicit (unbuffered Apply/Barrier are deterministic, the stuck-future risk is acknowledged by an in-repo TODO, a caller could bound the wait itself, and the select choice is a schedule rather than a data race) along with the unknowns (requests enqueued before shutdown, whether the GetConfiguration path shares the gap, and in-repo consumers). Optional preflight with the trusted validator returned valid=true; no target code was executed for this product, so the obligation is fixed but not yet checked.
